claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**How many children do you have, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex, who's 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 16 years old.

Since Alex is 16, there are some specific rules that apply. You can still qualify for Child Benefit if Alex is under 20 and stays in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, studying at school, college, or in approved training programs)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education at the moment. They finished school but haven't started anything else yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Since Alex is 16 and not currently in approved education or training, I need to ask a couple more questions:

**Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services?** 

(If Alex has registered within the last 20 weeks after leaving education, you may still be able to claim Child Benefit for that period)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't registered with any careers service or the armed services.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have a few more questions to make sure I have the complete picture:

**Is Alex currently working, and if so, how many hours per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't working at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Do you live in the UK, and does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester - and Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. Let me ask one final question to complete my assessment:

**Has Alex started claiming any benefits in their own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't claimed any benefits in their own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for answering all my questions. Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex at this time.

Here's why:

- Child Benefit is normally available for children under 16
- For children aged 16 or over, you can continue to receive Child Benefit if they stay in approved education or training (until they're 20)
- Since Alex is 16 and not currently in approved education or training, this condition isn't met
- Child Benefit can also continue for 20 weeks after a 16 or 17 year old leaves education if they register with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services, but Alex hasn't registered with either

**However, there may be options to regain eligibility:**

If Alex returns to approved education or training (such as college, sixth form, or an approved training program), you could become eligible for Child Benefit again. Also, if Alex registers with a careers service soon after leaving education, you might be able to claim for that 20-week period.

I hope this information is helpful. If Alex's circumstances change, you may want to reassess your eligibility.
